clue.text: Fighter's sporting misconduct reported after match

indicators.note: after places the sound-alike piece behind the word for match

parts.note: a match is a game, as of tennis or football

indicators.note: reported means the word for misconduct is given as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: a foul is an infringement of the rules in sport

explanation.surface: A boxer's dirty punch is talked about after the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns FOUL into FOWL, a word that sounds the same. 'Fighter's' is 'Fighter is', with the 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamecock or other bird bred for cockfighting is known by this name.

clue.text: Animal in Noah's Ark

parts.note: God told Noah to build the Ark of a particular wood that shares its name with a burrowing rodent

explanation.surface: A creature that went aboard Noah's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 6:14 has Noah build the Ark from this wood, so the animal is in the Ark as its timber, not as a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing North American rodent has the same name as the wood of the Ark.

clue.text: Tropical author

parts.note: a writer known for novels titled after the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn

explanation.surface: A writer from the hot countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tropical' suggests a writer from the tropics; it means the American novelist Henry Miller, author of Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Miller wrote Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

clue.text: Witty bishop covers a single sensitive area

indicators.note: covers means the bishop's letter sits on top of the word for one in this down entry

parts.note: funny means amusing or witty
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
one means a single

explanation.surface: An amusing bishop protects a tender part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'covers' puts B above ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The point at the elbow where the ulnar nerve is exposed tingles painfully when knocked.

clue.text: A specialist at 25, one who guards entrance?

definitions.meaning: 25 across is fielding; in cricket the keeper behind the stumps is the specialist fielder
a wicket is a small gate, so its keeper guards a way in

explanation.surface: A gatekeeper who is also expert at the cricket answer elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper is the fielder crouched behind the stumps; a wicket is also a small door or gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket player behind the stumps is the expert fielder, and a small-gate guard would be a gatekeeper of the wicket.

clue.text: French quack's source for rumour

definitions.meaning: the French word for a duck, the bird that quacks
an unfounded story or hoax report that sets gossip going

explanation.surface: A French charlatan is behind the latest gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word means duck, and in English it means a false, baseless report.

clue.text: A wife? Never wrong

parts.note: Miss is the title of a woman who has never married

explanation.surface: A question about marriage, firmly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS is the title for an unmarried woman, one who has never been a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order or faulty is said to be awry or not right.

clue.text: Like some vital passages from charter I altered

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A document changed so that some crucial passages are altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters running across 'charter I altered'. 'Vital passages' looks like key text in the charter; it means the blood vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Main blood vessels carrying blood from the heart, and major roads, share this adjective.

clue.text: Cross when upset, pots badly in part of opening frame

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for cross is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix

indicators.note: badly means the letters of pots are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooker player, annoyed, misses shots in the first frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ROOD into DOOR, and 'badly' rearranges POTS into POST. 'pots' and 'frame' suggest snooker, but the frame is a door's.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the upright timbers forming the sides of a doorway frame.

clue.text: Collar Merchant of Venice with audacity

parts.note: Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant and traveller
neck is British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: Shylock is collared for his impudence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant of Venice' points at Shakespeare's play, but here it means Marco Polo. NECK for cheek or nerve is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A high turned-over collar on a sweater gives the garment its name.

clue.text: I reached around painter

indicators.note: around means the phrase for reached is wrapped round the letter I

parts.note: got to means reached

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of putting their arms round an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the phrase GOT TO round I, which goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine fresco artist of the Scrovegni Chapel is an early Renaissance master.

clue.text: Supporter of the latest ad as TV rating collapses

indicators.note: collapses means the words ad as TV rating fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: A television ratings slump brings in fashionable advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' rearranges AD AS TV RATING.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate of new, experimental ideas in the arts is a champion of innovation.

clue.text: Soldiers in the old retreat — not ours

indicators.note: retreat means the assembled letters go backwards
in places the soldiers inside the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops of a bygone age fall back, and they are not on our side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns round the whole assembly, not just the soldiers. 'not ours' defines as an adjective-like phrase: the enemy's side is theirs, not ours.
explanation.definitionFit: The other side in a war is the opposing force, belonging to them rather than us.

clue.text: Overhear fall in Eden, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the fall in the Garden of Eden was Eve's, so it can be called Eve's drop

explanation.surface: A biblical question about what the Fall amounted to.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fall in Eden is pictured as 'Eve's drop', and 'say' turns EVE'S into EAVES, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen in secretly on others' conversation is the verb in question.

clue.text: Pupils that are industrious, though by no means noble

definitions.meaning: a group of school pupils, a class, who are hard at work
belonging to the labouring part of society, far from the aristocracy

explanation.surface: Hard-working schoolchildren who are certainly not aristocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent form of schoolchildren is one reading; the other is the social stratum of manual labourers, opposite to the peerage.

clue.text: Not a lot of money to recover, as gold is set on target

definitions.text: as gold is set on target

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value
to rally is to recover, as markets or patients do

explanation.surface: A small sum earned back as gold prices are propped up by investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' suggests the metal market; it is the gold ring at the centre of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold bull in archery lies in the middle of the target.

clue.text: One might get work on Times, for example, but not Mail, we hear

definitions.text: One might get work on Times, for example, but not Mail, we hear

parts.words: One might get work on Times, for example, but not Mail, we hear
parts.note: a woman in charge of a newspaper such as The Times, with Mail sounding like male, so the person is female

explanation.surface: A journalist's job hunt across Fleet Street newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times and the Daily Mail are British national newspapers; 'Mail' read aloud is male, so the newspaper boss is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female head of a publication, the old feminine form of a newspaper chief.

clue.text: Lie in bed, poorly, not fit to eat

indicators.note: poorly means the words lie in bed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick person in bed is off their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges LIE IN BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Food unsuitable for consumption is uneatable.

clue.text: Train leader after fool gets source of extra power

indicators.note: after puts the train leader's word behind the word for fool

parts.note: donkey means a stupid person
the engine is at the head of a train

explanation.surface: A railway story in which an idiot follows the locomotive and finds more power.
explanation.definitionFit: A small auxiliary steam motor used on ships for winches and pumps supplies additional force.

clue.text: Note article's extreme points

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Readers are told to spot the article's most extreme claims.
explanation.walkthrough: MINIM is the British name for a half note in music. The 's in 'article's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest values of a function or curve are its low points, plural of a mathematical term.

clue.text: Old Indian province bowled maiden, having put in England's openers

indicators.note: having put in means the opening letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled
a gal is a girl, an old word for a maiden

indicators.note: openers means the opening letters of the word England

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman bowled for a maiden after England's openers came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' takes the first two letters of England, and 'having put in' places them inside the other pieces. 'Bowled' and 'maiden' look like cricket terms, and B for bowled is indeed cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India, now split between India and Bangladesh.

clue.text: Toy manufactured at Derby — limited edition in it

indicators.note: in it means the shortened word goes inside the rearranged letters
manufactured means the words at Derby are made into something new

parts.note: ED is edition cut short, a standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soft toy is produced in a Derby factory in a small run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges the letters of 'at Derby', and 'in it' puts the edition abbreviation inside the rearranged run, after its first letter. Derby is an English industrial city.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed plush bear named after Theodore Roosevelt is a child's plaything.

clue.text: Country gets rid of striker with special delivery

definitions.meaning: Yorkshire, a large English county, often called God's Own Country, shortened

definitions.text: gets rid of striker with special delivery
definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl a batsman out with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet

explanation.surface: A nation disposes of a militant worker by recorded post.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, a county in northern England, is nicknamed God's Own Country. A yorker is a cricket ball aimed at the batsman's feet; the striker is the batsman facing.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated county name, and the verb for dismissing a batsman with a full-length ball aimed at the toes.

clue.text: Lower to the ground, say? Just the opposite

indicators.note: say means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to raze is to demolish a building completely, levelling it

explanation.surface: A request to knock something down, quickly reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns RAZE into a word that sounds the same, and that word means the reverse: to lift up rather than knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting up is the reverse of levelling a building to the ground.

clue.text: Board makes them quickly remove cover from branches

parts.note: em is them said in a hurry, with its start clipped
to bark a tree or branch is to strip its outer layer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to strip the trees in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link. BARK as a verb means to strip the bark off wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on a ship or plane is to go aboard.

clue.text: Author entering in a competition

definitions.meaning: an 18th-century English novelist, the writer of Tom Jones and Joseph Andrews
to field a team or candidate is to put it into a contest

explanation.surface: A writer submits work to a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones; to field a side is to put it forward in a contest.

clue.text: It's hard in part of ocean steamer for Jack's mate

indicators.note: in places the letter for hard inside the word for part of an ocean

parts.note: a sea is a portion of an ocean
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Something tough lies in a stretch of sea, where a sailor's partner rides a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a sailor (a jack tar), but here it is the male donkey, so his mate is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey, and the female donkey is its partner.

clue.text: Addition to rig of no help in the doldrums?

definitions.text: Addition to rig of no help in the doldrums?

parts.words: Addition to rig of no help in the doldrums?
parts.note: a sail on a ship's rigging that, in windless calm, stays where it is, doing nothing

explanation.surface: A ship's extra canvas is useless when the wind drops.
explanation.walkthrough: The doldrums are the calm belt near the equator where sailing ships lie becalmed; the clue jokes that any sail there would merely stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular fore-and-aft sail set on a stay is an extra piece of a ship's canvas.
